title: Windows PowerShell 5.1: the language and administration
description: From Get-Help and the pipeline to scripts, error handling, modules, remoting, security and DSC, with administration of services, processes, event logs, scheduled tasks, users and networking: Windows PowerShell 5.1 practised in a simulated PowerShell console on two pretend Windows machines. Our own syllabus, with notes where PowerShell 7 differs.
disclaimer: Cert Lab is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Microsoft. Microsoft, Windows, Windows Server and PowerShell are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. There is no single official PowerShell exam: this course follows a syllabus written for Cert Lab, and its practice exams are Cert Lab's own. The practice console is a simulation written by Cert Lab: it behaves like Windows PowerShell 5.1 for what the course covers, but it is not PowerShell, and nothing typed in it runs on this PC.
examNote: A Cert Lab practice exam: hands-on tasks on the two pretend Windows machines and multiple-choice questions, some of them "what does this print?". When you finish, the grader restarts both machines and checks them in a new PowerShell session, so your work must be saved where it survives: files, the registry, services, scheduled tasks, users, profiles and modules (variables and functions typed at the prompt are gone after a restart). Results are shown per unit. Some names and numbers change from one attempt to the next.
examHint: You are the administrator on both machines. Hands-on tasks: everything must survive a restart (the grader restarts WIN-SRV1 and WIN-CL1 first and opens a new PowerShell session). Questions: pick one answer. Points are shown with each item.
aboutMachines:
WIN-SRV1 (Windows Server 2022, 10.0.10.11) and WIN-CL1 (Windows 11, 10.0.10.21) are members of the pretend domain lab.example.com. DC01 (10.0.10.10) answers DNS and WEB01 (10.0.10.50) is a web server; they have no console. Each machine has a PowerShell console, started as the administrator in C:\Windows\system32, with services, processes, event logs, scheduled tasks, local users and groups, a registry, networking and sample files in C:\LabFiles.

The console is Cert Lab's own simulation of Windows PowerShell 5.1: the language (pipelines, objects, scripts, functions, errors), its default output, and the cmdlets the course uses. Commands it does not simulate say so. .NET types that could reach the real computer are refused. Remoting works between the two machines (WIN-CL1 needs Enable-PSRemoting first, as a real Windows client does), and background jobs and scheduled tasks follow the machines' clock.
